content_sections.heading: About DSLSA
content_sections.text: The Delhi State Legal Services Authority was set up under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, an Act of Parliament, and works under the administrative control of the High Court of Delhi. Its Central Office is on the 3rd Floor, Rouse Avenue District Court Complex, Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg, New Delhi-110002.

content_sections.heading: Work Profile
content_sections.text: Analytical study and research for future planning, so that the schemes of NALSA and DSLSA are implemented better. Support and assistance to victims in matters under the Delhi Victim Compensation Scheme in the District Legal Services Authorities. Legal assistance to victims of human trafficking, and looking after their welfare and rehabilitation together with NGOs working in the field. Preparing PowerPoint presentations, flyers, pamphlets, newsletters and information material for awareness and legal literacy programmes.

content_sections.heading: DSLSA Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: You must not have reached 27 years of age on the last date for receipt of applications, 16 November 2026. You must be a law graduate who passed the LL.B./Law Graduation degree after March 2023, with at least 60% marks. The degree must be from a Law School, College, University or Institution recognised by the Bar Council of India for enrolment as an Advocate. Final-year LL.B. students may also apply. They must show proof of having the law degree at the interview. If they cannot, they may not be called for interview and their application may be rejected. You need good knowledge of MS PowerPoint, Word and Excel. With your application form, you must attach a PowerPoint presentation of at least 15 slides on one of these research topics: Provisions of Legal Services Authorities Act - 1987 Research Methodology Victimology Victim Compensation Rights of under Trial Prisoners Rights of Children Right of Persons of LGBT Community You must meet every eligibility condition on the last date for applications. For the full eligibility conditions of the post, see the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: Candidates are selected on the basis of an interview only. No TA/DA is paid to candidates called for interview.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: Nature of engagement: a full-time job, but purely contractual and temporary. You cannot take up any other profession, service or engagement while you work for DSLSA. Period: the first engagement is for three months. It may be extended from time to time, up to a maximum of one year. Extensions depend on your work assessment, performance and conduct, and on what the Authority needs. No claim to a regular post: the engagement gives no right to a regular appointment or to continue in service at DSLSA. The Authority may end the engagement at any time without giving reasons. Leave: 12 days a year, with no more than 3 days in a calendar month. Leave above these limits is deducted pro rata from your pay. Leave you do not use cannot be carried forward to an extended period or encashed. Notice period: you must give one month's notice before leaving. Otherwise, one month's pay is deducted or recovered. Working hours: you may have to work beyond office hours, and no overtime is paid.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for DSLSA Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Go to the official website, www.dslsa.org . Open the web link for the Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant application. It is live from 2 November 2026, 10:00 AM to 16 November 2026, 5:00 PM. Fill in the online application form. Attach your PowerPoint presentation of at least 15 slides on one of the listed research topics. Submit the form before 5:00 PM on 16 November 2026. Applications sent any other way, such as a hard copy or by e-mail, will be rejected without consideration. Final-year students must bring proof of their law degree to the interview.

faq.question: Q1. Who can apply for the DSLSA Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant post?
faq.answer: You can apply if you passed your LL.B. after March 2023 with at least 60% marks from an institution recognised by the Bar Council of India. You must also be under 27 years of age on 16 November 2026.

faq.question: Q2. Can final-year LL.B. students apply?
faq.answer: Yes. However, they must show proof of having the law degree at the interview, or their application may be rejected.

faq.question: Q3. What is the salary of a DSLSA Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant?
faq.answer: The pay is a fixed consolidated Rs. 50,000 per month. Leave taken above 12 days a year or 3 days a month is deducted pro rata from this amount.

faq.question: Q4. What presentation do I need to attach?
faq.answer: You need a PowerPoint presentation of at least 15 slides on one listed topic, such as Victimology, Victim Compensation, Rights of Children or Rights of under Trial Prisoners.

faq.question: Q5. Can I apply by email or post?
faq.answer: No. You can apply only through the web link on www.dslsa.org. Hard-copy and e-mail applications will be rejected.

faq.question: Q6. How long does the engagement last?
faq.answer: It starts with three months and may be extended up to a maximum of one year, depending on your performance and the Authority's needs.

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected?
faq.answer: Selection is by interview only. Candidates called for interview are not paid any TA/DA.

faq.question: Q8. Can I do other work alongside this job?
faq.answer: No. This is a full-time assignment, and you cannot join any other profession, service or engagement while you work with DSLSA.

faq.question: Q9. What will a Law Clerk-cum-Research Assistant do?
faq.answer: The work includes research for NALSA and DSLSA schemes and help to victims under the Delhi Victim Compensation Scheme. It also covers legal help to victims of human trafficking and preparing material for legal literacy programmes.
